question: A term neonate is being resuscitated. After 30 seconds of effective PPV, the heart rate remains 50 bpm. Chest compressions are now started. Which of the following correctly describes the compression-to-ventilation ratio and the preferred technique for chest compressions in a neonate?

answers.text: 30:2 ratio using two-finger technique on the lower third of the sternum

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. 30:2 is the adult single-rescuer BLS ratio. In neonates, the ratio is 3:1 (3 compressions to 1 ventilation = 90 compressions + 30 breaths per minute). The two-finger technique is used when only one rescuer is present; the two-thumb encircling technique is preferred with two rescuers.

answers.text: 3:1 ratio using two-thumb encircling technique on the lower third of the sternum

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct! In neonatal resuscitation, chest compressions are given at a 3:1 ratio (3 compressions to 1 ventilation), yielding 90 compressions and 30 breaths per minute. The two-thumb encircling technique with fingers around the chest is preferred as it generates higher peak systolic pressure and is less tiring. Compressions are applied on the lower third of the sternum.

answers.text: 5:1 ratio using heel-of-hand technique over the mid-sternum

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. 5:1 is an older paediatric ratio no longer used in neonatal resuscitation. The NRP/HBB ratio is 3:1. The heel-of-hand technique is used in adults, not neonates. The correct neonatal technique is two thumbs with encircling fingers on the lower third of the sternum.

answers.text: 3:1 ratio using two-finger technique on the mid-sternum

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. The 3:1 ratio is correct, but there are two errors here. The landmark is the LOWER third of the sternum (one finger-breadth below the nipple line), not mid-sternum. The two-thumb encircling technique is preferred (two-finger is the alternative when encircling is not possible).

overallFeedback.feedback: The neonatal compression-to-ventilation ratio is 3:1 — unique to neonates because neonatal arrest is almost always hypoxic, so ventilation is equally prioritised with compression. Adult 30:2 does NOT apply. Two-thumb encircling technique on the lower third of the sternum is the preferred neonatal method.

Excellent! Key neonatal CPR facts: ratio 3:1 (vs adult 30:2), two-thumb encircling technique preferred, lower third of sternum, aiming for ~90 compressions + 30 breaths/min. Compressions are started when HR <60 bpm after 30 seconds of effective PPV.
